title: Remodeling Software: 6 Tools for Bids, Change Orders and Jobs
html:
Remodeling software has to cover three jobs: bid the work, run the project and get paid. JobTread covers estimates, proposals and change orders in one plan, Jobber suits crews that schedule more than they bid, and Joist and QuickBooks cover simple invoices and the books. Published prices run from $12 to $199 a month before extra users.

Remodeling software is different from the apps built for a one-visit trade, because a remodel runs for weeks and changes as it goes. A bathroom starts as a bid and ends with three change orders, two material selections and a punch list. This guide sorts six tools by the part of that cycle each one handles, with the price each vendor publishes and one real limit.

A remodeler can lose money in four places: a bid that missed a cost, a change that was never priced, a photo that was never taken, and an invoice that went out late. The tools below each close one of those gaps.

Which remodeling software handles bids, proposals and change orders?

JobTread is the project-based option here, and Joist is the light option for a crew that only needs estimates and invoices. Both put a price in front of the customer, but they go about it differently.

  • JobTread: its site describes budget templates, onscreen takeoff, supplier pricing, proposals with e-signatures and change orders tracked next to selections. It lists one plan at $199 a month with one user included, then $20 a month for each extra internal user from the second to the tenth. Customer and vendor portal users are free. Limit: the page lists no free trial, and the annual base price is not shown.
  • Joist: estimates, invoices and online payments. Basics is $12 a month billed monthly and Pro is $17. Limit: Basics allows 5 documents a month, and the free plan is no longer offered.

Bids and change orders are where remodeling profit leaks. A bid based on a gut feel hides a cost that appears at framing. A change order agreed in the driveway is never billed. Whatever tool you buy, set a rule that no extra work starts until the customer has approved a written price.

JobTread says customers can accept, deny or request changes on an estimate in a portal. That matters because it leaves a record. A customer who approved a $2,400 tile upgrade by signature does not argue about it at final payment. Ask any vendor to show you that approval trail in a demo.

Which remodeling software schedules crews and tracks jobs?

Jobber and JobTread both schedule work, but they start from different places. Jobber starts from the visit. JobTread starts from the project.

  • Jobber: scheduling, quotes, invoices and online payments. Core for one user is $49 a month with no commitment, or $29 a month billed annually, and Grow for one user is $199 a month with no commitment. Limit: extra users cost $29 a month each, and card payments carry a 2.9% plus 30 cents fee.

A remodeling company with two or three crews and a lot of short visits, such as estimates, measures and punch-list work, can fit Jobber well. A company that runs a few large projects at once and needs a budget per job will likely outgrow it. Test with a real project, not a demo job.

Which tool documents remodeling progress with photos?

CompanyCam documents job progress with photos, and it is the tool most remodelers will pay for first after estimating. Photos settle disputes and sell the next job.

  • CompanyCam: its site describes photo and video capture with unlimited cloud storage, annotations, project timelines, checklists, reports and integrations with QuickBooks and Jobber. Core is $63 a month and Crew is $129 a month, both billed annually, with extra users at $29 a month each. Limit: Core includes 10 AI credits and 5-minute videos, and the page lists no free plan.

Take photos at the same four points on every job: before demo, after demo, before cover-up and at completion. The shot before drywall covers the wiring and plumbing the customer will never see again. Months later, that photo answers a warranty question in seconds.

ToolJob it doesPublished priceReal limit
JobTreadBids, change orders, jobs$199 a month, 1 userNo free trial listed
JobberScheduling and invoices$49 monthly, $29 annual$29 per extra user
JoistEstimates and invoices$12 to $32 a month5 documents on Basics
CompanyCamJob photos and reports$63 to $199, billed annuallyAI credits capped on Core
QuickBooksAccounting$38 to $140 a monthPromo ends after 3 months
SketchUpDesign and layout$10.75 to $71.58 a monthGo is iPad and web only

Prices checked on each vendor page in November 2026. Annual prices are per month billed yearly.

Which tools handle remodeling design and accounting?

SketchUp handles design sketches and QuickBooks handles the books. They sit beside the project tool and rarely replace it.

  • SketchUp: a 3D modeling tool. Per user and billed annually, Go is $10.75 a month, Pro is $33.25 and Studio is $71.58, and prices exclude tax. Limit: Go is iPad and web only, and the page lists no general free plan.
  • QuickBooks: invoicing, bank feeds and reports. Simple Start is $38 a month, Essentials is $85 and Plus is $140, with promotional prices for the first three months. Limit: the free tier allows 2 invoices a month and 1 bank connection.

A 3D model helps a customer picture a layout, but it is not an estimate. Keep design and pricing apart, and do not let a pretty render promise a cost you have not checked. Accounting should match the job record, so ask what each project tool exports to QuickBooks.

What does one remodel look like in software from bid to final payment?

Walk one job through the stack before you buy. The path below shows where each tool touches the work.

  • Lead: a homeowner calls or fills in a form, and the request goes into your lead list the same day.
  • Site visit and bid: you measure, take photos and build a priced estimate from a template.
  • Proposal: the customer reviews scope, price and terms, then signs or asks for a change.
  • Production: the crew works from the schedule, and photos go into the job record at each stage.
  • Change orders: every added item gets a written price and a signature before work starts.
  • Invoice and review: a final invoice goes out on completion, and you ask for a review the same week.

If a tool cannot carry the job through all six steps without retyping, plan for a second tool to fill the gap. Retyping is where mistakes and late invoices come from.

What does a remodeling software stack cost?

A small remodeler can budget from about $50 to about $250 a month for software, depending on how much of the cycle is automated. The ranges below use only published prices.

  • Lean: Joist Basics at $12 a month and QuickBooks Simple Start at $38. Cost: $50 a month, plus card fees.
  • Middle: Jobber Core at $49 a month month to month, CompanyCam Core at $63 a month billed annually and QuickBooks Simple Start at $38. Cost: $150 a month before extra users.
  • Project-based: JobTread at $199 a month with one user, plus QuickBooks Simple Start at $38. Cost: $237 a month, with $20 for each extra internal user.

Compare those totals with one average job. If your typical remodel earns a few thousand dollars in profit, a tool that saves one missed change order a quarter has paid for itself. If it saves nothing, drop it.

How should a remodeler set up estimate templates?

Build one template per job type, not one giant list. A template saves time only when it matches the work you actually sell.

  • Start with your five most common jobs: such as a bath refresh, a kitchen update, a deck, a basement finish and a flooring swap.
  • List cost codes once: demo, framing, plumbing, electrical, drywall, finish and cleanup, so every bid reads the same way.
  • Add allowances for selections: tile, fixtures and cabinets get a stated allowance, and anything above it becomes a change order.
  • Include a clause for hidden conditions: rot, old wiring and uneven floors are priced when found, with written approval first.
  • Set a margin per line: JobTread says you can set target margins per item, so check that any tool you buy can do the same.

Review each template after every finished job. If a line ran over three times in a row, raise its price in the template. This is the cheapest profit fix in the business, and it needs no software upgrade, only discipline.

What mistakes do remodelers make when buying software?

Most remodeling software regrets come from buying too much too early. Four mistakes appear most often.

  • Buying the biggest plan first: a full project suite costs more per user and takes weeks to learn. Start with the stage that leaks the most money.
  • Skipping the trial job: run one live project through the tool before you commit. A demo job hides the awkward parts.
  • Ignoring card fees: a deposit of several thousand dollars on a 2.9% fee costs real money. Ask about bank transfer rates.
  • No owner for the data: pick one person to enter costs, upload photos and close out jobs. Shared ownership usually means no ownership.

Training matters as much as price. A crew lead who will not take photos turns CompanyCam into an expensive empty folder. Show the crew what the tool saves them, such as fewer callbacks, and ask them to try it on one job before you roll it out.

How do you choose remodeling software?

Choose remodeling software with a three-check filter: fit, cost and setup effort. Run every tool through all three before you sign.

Fit: does it price a bid by line item, track change orders and keep a record of customer approvals?

Cost: add the plan, extra users, card fees and add-ons, then compare against the profit on one average remodel.

Setup effort: can you build an estimate template and import customers in one weekend?

A one-crew remodeler fits Joist, CompanyCam and QuickBooks. A company that runs several projects at once fits a project tool such as JobTread. A crew that mostly does short visits can run on Jobber. Pilot one live job before moving the whole company.

What is the best software for a remodeling contractor?

A small remodeler can start with Joist and QuickBooks. A company running several large projects fits a project tool such as JobTread, which lists one plan at $199 a month with one user included.

How much does remodeling software cost?

Published plans in this guide run from $12 a month for Joist Basics to $199 a month for JobTread, and Jobber and CompanyCam sit between them. Extra users, card fees and add-ons cost more. A small stack can land near $50 to $250 a month.

Do remodelers need photo software?

Not on day one, but it pays off quickly. Photos settle disputes, document hidden work and give you material for reviews. CompanyCam lists Core at $63 a month billed annually, so compare that cost with one dispute you would otherwise lose.

Can Jobber run a remodeling business?

It can handle scheduling, quotes, invoices and payments, which suits crews with many short visits. Core for one user is $49 a month with no commitment. A company that tracks large project budgets and change orders should test it against a project tool first.

Is there free remodeling software?

Some tools have free tiers with tight limits. QuickBooks lists a free tier with 2 invoices a month and 1 bank connection. Many vendors have dropped free plans, such as Joist, so confirm current terms before you build a process around a free tool.

How do remodelers get more leads for their software to manage?

Leads come from local search, a clear website and reviews, not from project software. Start with a complete Google Business Profile and service pages for each remodel type. Then add search ads once your crew can handle the extra calls.

rot, old wiring and uneven floors are priced when found, with written approval first.
-
Set a margin per line:
JobTread says you can set target margins per item, so check that any tool you buy can do the same.
Review each template after every finished job. If a line ran over three times in a row, raise its price in the template. This is the cheapest profit fix in the business, and it needs no software upgrade, only discipline.
##
What mistakes do remodelers make when buying software?
Most remodeling software regrets come from buying too much too early. Four mistakes appear most often.
-
Buying the biggest plan first:
a full project suite costs more per user and takes weeks to learn. Start with the stage that leaks the most money.
-
Skipping the trial job:
run one live project through the tool before you commit. A demo job hides the awkward parts.
-
Ignoring card fees:
a deposit of several thousand dollars on a 2.9% fee costs real money. Ask about bank transfer rates.
-
No owner for the data:
pick one person to enter costs, upload photos and close out jobs. Shared ownership usually means no ownership.
Training matters as much as price. A crew lead who will not take photos turns CompanyCam into an expensive empty folder. Show the crew what the tool saves them, such as fewer callbacks, and ask them to try it on one job before you roll it out.
##
How do you choose remodeling software?
Choose remodeling software with a three-check filter: fit, cost and setup effort. Run every tool through all three before you sign.
Fit:
does it price a bid by line item, track change orders and keep a record of customer approvals?
Cost:
add the plan, extra users, card fees and add-ons, then compare against the profit on one average remodel.
Setup effort:
can you build an estimate template and import customers in one weekend?
A one-crew remodeler fits Joist, CompanyCam and QuickBooks. A company that runs several projects at once fits a project tool such as JobTread. A crew that mostly does short visits can run on Jobber. Pilot one live job before moving the whole company.
###
What is the best software for a remodeling contractor?
A small remodeler can start with Joist and QuickBooks. A company running several large projects fits a project tool such as JobTread, which lists one plan at $199 a month with one user included.
###
How much does remodeling software cost?
Published plans in this guide run from $12 a month for Joist Basics to $199 a month for JobTread, and Jobber and CompanyCam sit between them. Extra users, card fees and add-ons cost more. A small stack can land near $50 to $250 a month.
###
Do remodelers need photo software?
Not on day one, but it pays off quickly. Photos settle disputes, document hidden work and give you material for reviews. CompanyCam lists Core at $63 a month billed annually, so compare that cost with one dispute you would otherwise lose.
###
Can Jobber run a remodeling business?
It can handle scheduling, quotes, invoices and payments, which suits crews with many short visits. Core for one user is $49 a month with no commitment. A company that tracks large project budgets and change orders should test it against a project tool first.
###
Is there free remodeling software?
Some tools have free tiers with tight limits. QuickBooks lists a free tier with 2 invoices a month and 1 bank connection. Many vendors have dropped free plans, such as Joist, so confirm current terms before you build a process around a free tool.
###
How do remodelers get more leads for their software to manage?
Leads come from local search, a clear website and reviews, not from project software. Start with a complete Google Business Profile and service pages for each remodel type. Then add search ads once your crew can handle the extra calls.
